messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: POC trial plan & proposed models

Hi Carlos / Elena — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps for the FinLytics POC so we can get the trial running next week.

Summary of success criteria we heard today:
- Accuracy: >= 90% on the labeled QA/extraction set (100 curated prompts) for core financial entity extraction and classification.
- Latency: p95 inference < 350 ms for typical prompt sizes (see note on prompt lengths below).
- Cost: baseline unit cost target <= $X per 1K tokens (we'll refine once we have tokenized samples).
- Multilingual: robust English + Spanish support (Portuguese is a "nice-to-have" for round 2).

Proposed model selection for the trial (recommendation):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized q4o) — best cost/quality tradeoff for instruction-following tasks and structured extraction.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized q4o) — use for edge cases where higher-context reasoning improves accuracy (e.g., multi-sentence reconciliation).

Why this combo: Mistral-7B gives fast throughput and competitive instruction quality; Llama-2-13B-chat can be used as a higher-capacity fallback for prompts that fail confidence thresholds. Both are available in our model catalog and compatible with Redwood runtime optimizations (KV/prefix caching + quantized kernels).

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Nov 23: POC kickoff + access to Redwood trial workspace. FinLytics to upload sample prompt set (we requested sample_prompt_set.csv).
- Nov 25–26: Baseline runs (both models) on the 100+ evaluation prompts.
- Nov 29–Dec 3: Evaluation week — collect accuracy metrics, latency, hallucination/QA checks.
- Dec 6: Decision week — review results and propose next steps (Dedicated capacity or hosted plan).

Ownership:
- FinLytics: provide labeled sample prompts (200 representative examples ideally) and pass/fail labels by Nov 24.
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) will coordinate kickoff and procurement items; Ben (SE) will run the model baselines and provide perf/latency reports; Rishi (CS) will own onboarding and success criteria tracking.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm the model selection above (Mistral-7B primary / Llama-2-13B-chat fallback) or flag any preferences.
2) Upload sample_prompt_set.csv to the Drive link and confirm dataset delivery by COB Nov 23.
3) If you have any regulatory/security constraints (SOC2, IP restrictions), send those docs — we have included our SOC2 snapshot in the attachments as well.
4) Confirm kickoff time (I proposed Nov 23 10:00am PST below).

Attachments: FinLytics_POC_requirements.docx, sample_prompt_set.csv, SOC2_snapshot.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hi all — quick technical notes on the recommended stack and perf expectations so the team can set realistic targets.

Model & infra guidance:
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4o) running on A100/80GB-equivalent in Redwood runtime: expect p50 ~60–90ms, p95 ~250–350ms depending on prompt length and batching. Great cost profile for high QPS.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (q4o) as fallback: p50 ~120–180ms, p95 ~350–500ms (higher mem usage but better for longer-context reasoning).

Recommendations to meet p95 < 300ms where possible:
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes (we can cache recent invoice templates/boilerplate).
- Start with batch size = 1–2 for latency-sensitive runs; use larger batches for offline bulk evals.
- Use top-k/top-p tuning and confident-score thresholds to route low-confidence cases to the 13B fallback.

Data ask: please include average prompt length (tokens and characters) and worst-case examples. For multilingual behavior, include Spanish prompts with expected labels.

I've attached a quick model_perf_estimates.xlsx with microbenchmarks and config suggestions. I can run a baseline once we have the sample_prompt_set.csv in Drive.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
